# Binary oversampling research progress

## Full remaining-dataset extension - frozen before outcomes

User requests the remaining datasets with SVM/KNN only and one final comparison
averaged across both classifiers. LR/RF are excluded from this extension and the
default CLI classifier list is now SVM/KNN; historical results are preserved.

Inventory: 44 folders, 42 numeric datasets. Six already have the matched revised
SVM/KNN experiment. Run the other 36 with exactly the same nine methods, two seeds
(42,137), five supplied folds, ratios [0.5,0.75,1.0], training-only 25% stratified
holdout selection on mean G-mean/F1, and default prediction thresholds. No sampler
parameter or model changes based on the remaining test results. Exclude abalone19
and abalone9-18 because their Sex input is categorical; one-hot interpolation or
categorical snapping would change the method, so neither is silently substituted.

Tiny-data feasibility rule: KNN uses min(7, number of resampled training observations)
for every sampler. This prevents invalid prediction when RUS leaves fewer than seven
observations; it does not change any of the earlier six-dataset results. The effective
neighbor count is recorded. SVM stays RBF C=1, gamma=scale, KNN distance-weighted.

The same 36-dataset extension comprises 6480 outer fits plus up to 17280 inner
ratio trials. The report will show remaining-only and all-42 numeric averages,
equal-weight per dataset then per classifier, per-classifier means, and pairwise
and joint win/tie/loss counts. A dataset with any failed or missing method/model
cell is excluded from the matched aggregate for ALL methods and explicitly listed.
No failed method is replaced by a different sampler. Run checkpoints permit resume
at dataset boundaries without adding files. Complete raw errors remain in this log.

Remaining does not mean fully independent: some of these datasets were examined
in earlier UGA/LocalMargin experiments; several KEEL tasks share source families.
An empirical win supports performance in this setting, not proof of novelty.
The method combines source allocation, SMOTE interpolation and established ENN;
a dedicated prior-art review is required before a novelty claim.

Prior-art sanity check during this run: the official imbalanced-learn documentation
already describes SMOTE followed by ENN cleaning and points to earlier research.
Thus better scores do not demonstrate that combining oversampling and cleaning is
new. Candidate-specific source allocation must be compared with closely matched
SMOTE + majority-only ENN controls before attributing gains to the CASB design.
Current SMOTE-ENN uses its library-default cleaning settings, so it is a useful
strong baseline but not a fully matched cleaning-only ablation.
Source: https://imbalanced-learn.org/stable/combine.html

## Latest result: edited CASB with SVM and KNN

**Completed 19 October 2026:** 1080 outer model fits, zero failures. Two seeds,
five supplied folds, six datasets, SVM and KNN, nine methods. Each of the eight
resampling methods received three additional training-only ratio trials per outer
setting (2880 inner fits; 3960 fits total). Objective: (G-mean + minority F1)/2.

`casb_edited` is the strongest candidate in this development study. It uses broader
70/20/10 source coverage, unrestricted same-class interpolation, followed by
majority-only 3-neighbor ENN majority-vote cleaning. Original minority examples
are retained. `casb_relaxed` omits cleaning and was weaker. This supports the value
of cleaning within this tested configuration, not a general causal claim about ENN.

| Comparator | Edited CASB wins / ties / losses across six datasets |
|---|---:|
| SMOTE | 4 / 1 / 1 |
| Borderline-SMOTE | 5 / 1 / 0 |
| ROS | 4 / 1 / 1 |
| RUS | 5 / 0 / 1 |

Counts use composite scores after equally averaging SVM/KNN, folds and seeds.
**Pairwise majority wins are achieved against each baseline separately. The stricter
predeclared goal of beating all four on the same dataset in at least 4/6 datasets
is NOT achieved:** joint wins are 3/6 (Pima, Haberman, Ecoli4). Only Pima and
Haberman improve both individual metrics against all four. Ecoli4 trades G-mean
against F1 relative to RUS, and no resampling has the highest composite there.
Yeast3 favors RUS. Segment0 favors SMOTE/ROS. Vowel0 ties several methods near the
ceiling, so ties are not counted as wins. Separately, joint composite wins are
2/6 with SVM and 3/6 with KNN; model averaging must not hide these counts.

| Method | Mean G-mean | Mean minority F1 | Composite |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Edited CASB | 0.8624 | 0.7767 | 0.8195 |
| SMOTE-ENN | 0.8551 | 0.7681 | 0.8116 |
| Original CASB | 0.8453 | 0.7565 | 0.8009 |
| SMOTE | 0.8419 | 0.7572 | 0.7995 |
| Borderline-SMOTE | 0.8453 | 0.7504 | 0.7979 |

These scores are comparable within this tuned SVM/KNN study, not directly with the
earlier fixed-ratio LR/RF table. All settings and failed/non-winning cases remain
documented below. The candidate was designed using prior results on these datasets;
new untouched datasets are required before an independent superiority claim.
Single inner holdout, small dataset count, related families and shared duplicate
feature vectors remain limitations. No statistical significance or novelty claim.

## Active revision study: SVM and KNN (19 October 2026)

User now explicitly authorizes CASB modifications, aiming to beat SMOTE, BSMOTE,
ROS and RUS on a majority of datasets. This supersedes the earlier instruction to
leave CASB unchanged when any improvements were observed.

Frozen revision candidates before this run: `casb_relaxed` uses source weights
70% coverage / 20% border / 10% rare and removes short interpolation limits;
`casb_edited` adds majority-only 3-neighbor ENN majority-vote cleaning after that
generation. All original minority observations are retained. These are combinations
of established mechanisms, not a claim of a novel cleaning algorithm. Their direct
comparison isolates cleaning; changes to coverage and margins are bundled, so this
run does not separately establish which of those two changes causes a difference.

Models: RBF SVM C=1, gamma=scale; distance-weighted KNN k=7. Identical model settings
for every sampler. SVM uses decision scores for AP/AUC, not probability calibration.
Dataset set unchanged: pima, haberman, yeast3, ecoli4, vowel0, segment0. These are
now development benchmarks, not pristine confirmation data. Five provided outer
folds, seeds 42 and 137. Every sampler gets the same ratio grid [0.50,0.75,1.00],
selected on the same stratified 25% split of outer-training data. Preprocessing
is refit inside validation and then on the full outer training partition.
No classifier threshold tuning. Selection objective: (G-mean + minority F1)/2;
the raw validation `ba` field stores this selected objective for this tagged run.
Lower ratio breaks validation ties. Post-ENN class counts are explicitly recorded;
the requested ratio applies before cleaning, as in SMOTE-ENN comparisons.

Primary majority-win definition: average fold/seed scores within each model and
dataset, then average SVM/KNN equally; revised method must exceed each of the four
core baselines on the composite score in at least 4 of 6 datasets. Also report
separate classifier results and the stricter requirement of improving BOTH metrics.
No test-result parameter changes during this run. Two candidates are reported
separately; selecting the better one afterward is exploratory, not confirmation.

Validation passed: original CASB invariants; revision reproducibility, same-class
interpolation reconstruction, original-minority preservation, majority-only editing,
and actual SVM/KNN fits for all required methods. The earlier approval usage-limit
block is resolved. Six existing notebooks will retain prior LR/RF results and receive
an additional executed section for this study; no build or dependency directory added.

## Scope and success rule - 19 October 2026

Keep one reusable implementation (`binary_oversampling.py`) and this report only.
Source: supplied seven-page `Custom_SMOTE_Based_Oversampling_Pipeline.pdf`, read in full.
Goal: investigate improvement over SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE (borderline-1), ROS and RUS;
no guarantee of superiority and no fabricated results. Original, class weighting,
ADASYN, SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek are additional controls.

Primary metric: balanced accuracy. Secondary: minority F1, average precision (AP),
G-mean, ROC AUC, minority precision/recall, specificity, macro/weighted F1, confusion
matrix and runtime. AP is average precision, not trapezoidal PR AUC. All methods
use identical original KEEL five-fold splits, training-only median imputation and
standardization, and identical classifiers: logistic regression or random forest
(100 trees, minimum leaf size 2). Predictions use the default classifier rule.
No test data enter preprocessing, resampling, source scoring or hyperparameter selection.

Development datasets fixed before seeing results: pima, haberman, glass1, yeast3.
Reserved next-stage datasets: vehicle1, ecoli2, new-thyroid1, page-blocks0.
Other datasets are not benchmarked in this initial task. Some related benchmark
families are correlated; results cannot establish universal superiority.

Pilot: one seed (42), all five supplied folds, both classifiers, fixed full-balance
target. No tuning. This screens ideas; it is not a final statistical claim.
If the PDF method is uncompetitive, develop one alternative using development
results and then freeze it before touching the reserved datasets. Any further
comparison with ratio tuning must give every resampling method the same candidate
ratios and training-only validation split. Favor consistent dataset-level gains
over a single favorable fold or a single pooled average.

## PDF implementation decisions

- Binary minority label is derived from each training partition, not global data.
- Logistic-regression selection model uses original training data without class weights.
- Maximum-probability uncertainty and cluster-size rarity are separately min-max normalized.
- KMeans cluster count: min(5, max(2, floor(sqrt(n_minority/2)))), capped by unique points.
- Top 25% sources; alpha 0.5; 5 same-class neighbours; 10 overlap neighbours.
- Full method accepts overlap <=0.5 and intended-class probability >= training minority prior.
  These are predeclared pilot defaults, not optimal values or thresholds specified by the PDF.
- Uniform SMOTE interpolation; maximum attempts 20 times the requested synthetic count.
  Underfilled targets are reported; no hidden random oversampling fallback.
- All four PDF ablations are implemented. Full candidate logs stay in the sampler's
  `audit_` attribute; aggregate audits and raw fold results are persisted here to
  respect the user's minimal-file requirement. Candidate logs can be regenerated
  using recorded code/configuration/seed; they are not individually saved to disk.
- Numeric binary KEEL/ARFF and CSV inputs supported. Nominal features are rejected
  explicitly; adding correct mixed-type geometry/SMOTENC is separate work.
- Standard baselines use the official imbalanced-learn implementations:
  https://imbalanced-learn.org/stable/over_sampling.html
  https://imbalanced-learn.org/stable/references/generated/imblearn.over_sampling.BorderlineSMOTE.html

## Completed development stage and frozen next experiment

Inventory: 44 folders, 42 numeric binary datasets and two nominal-feature Abalone
datasets. Alternate KEEL filename spelling in new-thyroid2 is handled. Correctness
checks passed for reproducibility, input immutability, same-class neighbors,
interpolation reconstruction, acceptance criteria, balanced/string labels, and
execution of every baseline. No pilot failures among 520 outer-fold fits.

Pilot equal-weight average balanced accuracy across four datasets x two models:
UGA-full 0.7202, SMOTE 0.7365, BSMOTE 0.7371, ROS 0.7480, RUS 0.7515.
UGA-full does improve over the unresampled reference (0.6921), but does not beat
the required controls. Its AP is relatively strong (0.6682), illustrating metric
tradeoffs; this does not override the predeclared primary metric.
All UGA targets were filled, so the observed degradation is not target underfill.
The ablations support dropping this particular top-fraction/filter combination;
they do not prove every possible UGA hyperparameterization will fail.

Revision: **LocalMarginSMOTE** (`margin`), uniform source coverage, ordinary
same-class nearest neighbors, but lambda ~ Uniform(0, min(1, 0.5*d_major/edge_length)).
d_major is the source's nearest observed majority distance. This limits long
interpolation through majority regions. By the triangle inequality, a candidate
is no farther from its minority source than from any observed majority point.
That geometric property does not establish the candidate's true label.
Coincident opposing labels produce duplicate points (zero step), explicitly audited.
No global uncertainty model, rare-cluster priority, source deletion or hard rejection.
This is an exploratory combination of established ideas, not a proven novel algorithm.
The motivation is consistent with the official guide's discussion of SMOTE
connecting inliers/outliers and ADASYN emphasizing outliers:
https://imbalanced-learn.org/stable/over_sampling.html#smote-variants

Two variants tested on development data only (80 further outer-fold fits):
uniform `margin`: BA 0.7538, F1 0.6356, AP 0.6687;
soft reliability-weighted `margin_reliable`: BA 0.7447, F1 0.6257, AP 0.6629.
Choose uniform `margin` because of development BA. Its gain over the strongest
aggregate control RUS is only ~0.23 percentage points; this is exploratory selection,
not independent confirmation. Reliability weighting is not the selected method.
Margin invariant checks passed, including nearest-majority distance guarantee.

Frozen before reserved-data evaluation: margin_fraction=0.5, k=5, uniform sources,
full-balance target, original classifiers unchanged, seeds [42, 137, 2026]. Run
vehicle1, ecoli2, new-thyroid1, page-blocks0 on all five supplied folds with all nine
controls and margin. No post-result parameter or threshold changes permitted in
this confirmation stage. No ratio tuning is applied to any method in this stage.

Data caveat: supplied folds in Haberman and Yeast3 share exact feature vectors
between training and test (maximum 11 distinct vectors in a fold). The original
benchmark splits are preserved for every method; duplicate-group-disjoint sensitivity
evaluation is needed before strong generalization claims. Overlap counts are saved.

## Classifier expansion: RF, LR, GaussianNB

Both 44-dataset benchmark and 20-seed overlap simulation. Fixed existing sampler settings. Five supplied folds and seeds 42/137 for benchmark; separations 5 to 0 for overlap. Train-only 25% holdout selects ratio .5/.75/1 by (G-mean + F1)/2; lower ratio breaks ties. RF: 100 trees, min leaf 2; LR: default C=1, max_iter=3000; GaussianNB: var_smoothing=1e-9. No classifier tuning, no test-set selection. All failures retained. No notebook or figure changes.

## Classifier expansion: RF, LR, GaussianNB

Both 44-dataset benchmark and 20-seed overlap simulation. Fixed existing sampler settings. Five supplied folds and seeds 42/137 for benchmark; separations 5 to 0 for overlap. Train-only 25% holdout selects ratio .5/.75/1 by (G-mean + F1)/2; lower ratio breaks ties. RF: 100 trees, min leaf 2; LR: default C=1, max_iter=3000; GaussianNB: var_smoothing=1e-9. No classifier tuning, no test-set selection. All failures retained. No notebook or figure changes.
